correctness.rationale: Strict leftness gives det(v_i,v_{i+1})>0, so the signed principal increment is the unique arccos branch in (0,pi). A segment between the two rays stays within their positive cone, so this is also its continuous lifted change of argument. The origin is interior, and simplicity and counterclockwise orientation give winding one; the increments really sum to 2pi. The radii and cumulative angles give the full Gram entry by the cosine of their difference. An adjacent pair is a basis and equality of its Gram matrix defines an orthogonal map; inner products with that basis then identify all remaining vertices. A color-preserving cyclic shift retains the orientation, while a color-preserving reversal can be composed with a reflection to restore counterclockwise orientation before applying the same completion. Conversely a polygon symmetry preserves the boundary's cyclic adjacency (vertices are genuine corners) and the local scalars. The alternating-radius hexagon has positive consecutive determinants and alternating turn signs, and its consecutive angular sectors show simplicity. The proof covers all stated n, including n=3, and is not uniqueness among unconstrained rank-two completions. The supplied NumPy checker was inspected, not executed; its reported 792 configurations and 22,932 candidate permutations are diagnostics and do not establish the exact theorem.
